name: Redline Combat Ankle Sheath
description:
A neoprene ankle wrap with an integrated sheath for a fixed-blade knife up to 12cm. The sheath holds the blade handle-down for a cross-draw from a kneeling or crouching position. The neoprene wrap is breathable, moisture-wicking, and sits comfortably under boots or pant legs without printing.

The last-resort carry option for people who assume their primary weapon will eventually be taken from them. The ankle sheath is uncomfortable on long walks and obvious to anyone who knows what to look for, but it has saved lives in situations where everything else was already gone.
functionality: Concealed blade carry, cross-draw positioning, last-resort weapon access
what_it_says: You plan for the moment when everything else has been taken and you're down to what's on your ankle.
story_hooks: An ankle sheath is found with the knife missing but the sheath's interior coated in a substance that isn't blood — whatever was sheathed here wasn't a standard blade.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting ankle wrap that hugs the lower leg with a subtle bulge on the inner ankle where the sheath sits. The integrated blade pocket creates minimal visual disruption, appearing as a natural contour of the wrap rather than an obvious weapon carrier. When worn under boots or tapered pants, it reads as functional compression gear rather than tactical equipment.
physical_description.fit: Compression-fit around the ankle and lower calf, secured with adjustable closures that allow customization for different boot heights and leg sizes. Sits snugly enough to prevent shifting during movement but loose enough for all-day wear without cutting off circulation.
physical_description.primary_material: High-grade neoprene blend with moisture-wicking synthetic interior lining and reinforced ballistic weave on the sheath pocket itself
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly tacky neoprene exterior; ribbed interior for grip and comfort against skin; the sheath area has a subtle quilted texture for blade retention
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal gray base with red accent stitching along the sheath seam and a small Redline Combat crimson logo patch on the outer ankle. Some variants feature black-on-black for deeper concealment.
physical_description.closures: Medical-style velcro straps with friction-fit reinforcement at the top and bottom; magnetic micro-closure on sheath flap for silent blade access
distinctive_features: Handle-down blade orientation allows cross-draw from crouching/kneeling positions
Seamless integration with standard combat boots
Red accent stitching visible under pant leg when worn
Reinforced ballistic panel surrounding sheath pocket
Designed to sit underneath pant leg without obvious printing
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional working class to street operative; affordable tactical gear for people who can't afford corpo-grade redundancy systems
physical_description.cultural_context: Street soldiers, maintenance workers, underleveled corp security, anyone operating in mid-tier conflict zones. Signals preparedness, street smarts, and assumption of violence. Worn by people who've learned the hard way that primary weapons get compromised.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-broken-in with visible wear patterns on the velcro, scuffed neoprene from boot friction, and slight discoloration from sweat stains that resist full cleaning. The red stitching often fades slightly from UV exposure.
